notes: The San Francisco Call's daily Building Contracts list for 1912, printed in the Real Estate Transactions column, read from curiv_angwin_ver02, curiv_calipatria_ver03 and curiv_dardanelle_ver01 (9,693 OCR pages; no issue after 15 December 1912 is in any batch). Located by the same two passes as 1911 - the list's heading, which the OCR mangles ('Ruildins: Contract*', 'Bntldlng Contract*'), and the entry's own shape ('with CONTRACTOR - WORK ... line/corner of ...; $AMOUNT') - merged into page-blocks trimmed at the first long gap between contract amounts; each block read by hand into structured fields. A contract reprinted later is kept once, at its first printing (extra.reprinted); contracts reprinted on two pages of one issue are kept once. Private owners, trustees, estates named for a person and partnerships of surnames are cut from address_as_written, raw and extra; institutional and company owners are kept in extra.owner_firm, contractors in extra.contractors and any architect in extra.architect. Every entry carries extra.record_date (1912 is after the 1909 renumbering). Placed with research/tools/corner.py's geometry (dir mode for line entries, the corner radius for corner entries) with a street's EAS type carried through - corner.py now takes '08TH AVE' / '08TH ST', because EAS files a numbered street and avenue under one name. A placement needs a single parcel matching the roll year within two years and, where the record gives them, the offset within 4 ft and the lot area within 4%; its EAS point on the side of the street, or in the quadrant of the corner, the record names; a storey count within one and a half of the record's; and a parcel on the current roll. Hand placements carry by_hand with the measurement in method. Pure renames applied for geometry only: First avenue = Arguello, Army = Cesar Chavez, Dupont = Grant, the lettered Sunset and Richmond streets of 1909 (A = Anza, B = Balboa, I = Irving, J = Judah, L = Lawton, N = Noriega, P = Pacheco, T = Taraval), Thirteenth avenue = Funston, H street = Lincoln way. A street number printed on a renamed lettered street is not trusted. Where several contracts name the same building, the general contract (else the earliest) carries the page's entry and the others are declined as folded into it.

coverage.remaining: Nothing of the 1912 lists is known to remain unread. 32 entries match several parcels with nothing in the record to choose between them and 82 single candidates were refused (the wrong side of the street for 67); 81 could not be measured (streets that no longer meet, expunged alleys, a direction that does not run along the street). 1913's lists are next: its batches hold 1-15 February and 16 July-8 December only.
coverage.note: 9,693 OCR pages scanned; 507 page-blocks held the list or something shaped like it (253 of them with no contract entry - deeds columns, building-loan news, ads); 1,388 contract entries read, of which 73 were fragments cut off at a block's end with no location or amount, and 13 were reprints (9 within an issue, 4 in a later issue) - 1,302 findings (1,164 building contracts, 138 alterations). 209 resolved - 199 by corner, offset and lot with corner.py's geometry, 10 by a printed street number - and 1,093 unresolved: 729 whose corner or block face has no parcel matching the record's lot or offset with a roll year near 1912, 82 single candidates refused (67 on the wrong side of the street or corner, 8 retired parcels, 7 storey counts), 32 matching several parcels, 81 whose streets could not be measured, 75 on streets that could not be matched to an EAS street (expunged alleys such as Ecker, Webb, Chelsea place, and OCR-mangled names), 35 located only by a tract block or lot, 22 with no cross street, 19 with no legible location, 13 printed numbers with no EAS record, 3 numbers held back (two garbled, one on a renamed lettered street) and 1 condominium parcel. 166 published on 166 pages, 107 of them seeded; 43 declined - 35 folded into another contract for the same building, 4 on parcels rebuilt since, 4 trade contracts (painting, plumbing) that say nothing a reader needs.
